proof:
# Every nonvertex fiber strictly improves its own ordinary maximal depth

Let d>=1 and let a compact convex set C induce finitely many positive
full-dimensional fibers K_p in R^d, indexed by P subset Z^n. Let mu be
summed d-volume on these fibers. Additional zero-d-volume fibers do not
change mu and are irrelevant to this statement. For w in P define the
**absolute**, unnormalized quantities

    A(K_w)=max_(g in K_w) inf_(u in S^(d-1))
                         |K_w intersect {u dot (x-g)>=0}|,

    A_mu(w)=max_(y in K_w) inf_(closed ambient H containing (w,y)) mu(H).

Then

    A_mu(w)=A(K_w)       if w is a vertex of conv(P),
    A_mu(w)>A(K_w)       if w is not a vertex of conv(P).       (1)

In particular every nonvertex satisfies

    A_mu(w)>Gamma_d |K_w|,  Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.               (2)

More strongly, an explicit interior point and an explicit gain are given
below. This is a local comparison to the actual ordinary maximal depth,
not a global mixed-depth lower bound in terms of total source mass. It
does not prove OC. There is no assertion for d=0 or for fibers of differing
intrinsic continuous dimensions.

The local proof uses only ordinary continuous Grunbaum for the shape-only
corollary. It does not use ordinary simplex rigidity, mixed-cap attainment,
a classification of active normals, or any lower-integer OC hypothesis.
The final limited-cardinality equality classification separately invokes
the already proved ordinary simplex-rigidity theorem.
Archive checks found the related one-fiber deletion and critical-cap
lemmas, but not this strict local comparison.

## 1. Quantitative anchored-source lemma

The base points in this lemma can even be real. Fix distinct p_1,...,p_k,
all different from w, and positive lambda_i summing to one, with

    sum_i lambda_i p_i=w.

Let their positive d-dimensional convex fibers and K_w satisfy the actual
compatibility inclusion

    E=sum_i lambda_i K_(p_i) subset K_w.                     (3)

Write mu_0 for volume on just these k+1 fibers. Any additional positive
measure may be added to mu_0 in the conclusion.

Choose an ordinary deepest point g of K_w, and write A=A(K_w). Suppose

    B_d(g,r) subset K_w,    B_d(m,rho) subset E,

where r,rho>0. Assume each of the k+1 fibers lies in a Euclidean ball of
radius R>0; the containing balls need not have the same center. Let

    nu=min(|K_w|,|K_(p_1)|,...,|K_(p_k)|)>0,
    omega=|B_2^(d-1)|, with omega=1 when d=1,
    L=(k+1) omega R^(d-1),
    delta=nu (rho/(4R))^d,
    epsilon=min(1/2, r/(4R), delta/(4RL)),
    c=omega (r/2)^(d-1),
    G=min(delta/2, c epsilon rho/2)>0.                        (4)

Because E subset K_w and each lies in a radius-R ball where relevant,
r,rho<=R and |m-g|<=2R. In particular all quantities in (4) are finite.
Set

    y=g+epsilon(m-g).                                       (5)

Then y is in int(K_w), and every ambient closed halfspace H containing
(w,y) satisfies

    mu_0(H)>=A+G.                                           (6)

Thus the statement controls all integer tilts and all continuous normals
simultaneously. No constants depend on the magnitudes of the p_i or on a
positive lower bound for the lambda_i.

### Proof: the exact cancellation of integer tilts

Put v=m-g. It is enough first to consider a nonvertical cap through
(w,y), normalized to have unit continuous normal u. Its parallel cap
through (w,g) has margin

    L_g(p,x)=a dot (p-w)+u dot (x-g).

Let

    b_i=max_(x in K_(p_i)) L_g(p_i,x)
       =a dot (p_i-w)+h_(K_(p_i))(u)-u dot g.

The same integer tilt a appears at every source. The base first-moment
identity gives the exact support cancellation

    sum_i lambda_i b_i=h_E(u)-u dot g
                      >=u dot v+rho.                       (7)

This is where the anchored incidence is used. The individual b_i need
not have the same sign, and the conclusion never replaces a common tilt
by independently chosen fiber tilts.

Suppose first that u dot v>=-rho/2. Equation (7) implies b_i>=rho/2 for
at least one i. Let x_i maximize this margin. The homothetic copy

    (1-t)x_i+t K_(p_i),  t=rho/(4R)<=1,

lies in the cap L_g>=0. Indeed every directional width of K_(p_i) is at
most 2R, so all its points have margin at least b_i-2Rt>=0. Therefore
this source fiber contributes at least t^d |K_(p_i)|>=delta, while the
own-fiber cap contributes at least A. Thus

    mu_0{L_g>=0}>=A+delta.                                  (8)

Moving the candidate to (5) changes the common scalar threshold by
`epsilon u dot v`. Each body's hyperplane sections have (d-1)-volume at
most omega R^(d-1), since it lies in a radius-R ball. Integrating these
sections shows that any parallel threshold displacement of magnitude h
changes mu_0 cap mass by at most Lh, for every tilt a. Consequently

    mu_0(H)>=A+delta-L epsilon |v|>=A+delta/2.                (9)

The last inequality uses |v|<=2R and epsilon<=delta/(4RL).

Suppose instead that u dot v<-rho/2. Moving g to y lowers the cap
threshold by q=-epsilon u dot v>epsilon rho/2. Every source cap grows.
Moreover q<=epsilon |v|<=r/2. In the own ball B_d(g,r), each section at
signed distance between -q and zero has area at least

    omega (r/2)^(d-1)=c.

For d=1 this statement means simply that interval length added equals q.
The own-fiber slab therefore adds at least cq, giving

    mu_0(H)>=A+c epsilon rho/2.                              (10)

Equations (9)--(10) prove (6) for every nonvertical through-point cap.
Any larger nonvertical containing cap contains its parallel cap through
the candidate, so the same conclusion holds for it.

A vertical containing cap includes the whole own fiber. Since ordinary
opposite caps sum to |K_w|, A<=|K_w|/2. Also delta<=nu<=|K_w|, so
G<=delta/2<=|K_w|/2. Hence its mass is at least |K_w|>=A+G. All vertical
closed caps are covered, including ones containing boundary base fibers.
Finally (5) is a convex combination of g and m in K_w with
1-epsilon>=1/2; the interior ball at g shows y is interior. This proves
(6), including the possible case m=g, when only the first normal regime
occurs.

## 2. Proof of strict improvement at every nonvertex

If w is a nonvertex of conv(P), Caratheodory gives an anchored
representation using k<=n+1 other bases, with positive coefficients
after zero terms are discarded. Convexity of C gives (3). All chosen
fibers have positive d-volume, so their Minkowski combination E is
full-dimensional and contains some ball B_d(m,rho).

An ordinary deepest point g of K_w exists and is interior. For
completeness, ordinary cap masses are jointly continuous in the unit
normal and candidate, because their boundary hyperplanes have zero
volume. Minimization over the compact unit sphere gives a continuous
depth function. Outside or on the boundary of K_w a supporting cap has
zero volume, whereas an interior ball gives positive depth. Hence its
positive maximum is attained in the interior. Choose r>0 with
B_d(g,r) subset K_w and a finite R containing the finitely many selected
bodies as above. The quantitative lemma gives

    A_mu(w)>=A_mu0(w)>=A(K_w)+G>A(K_w).

Ordinary Grunbaum supplies A(K_w)>=Gamma_d|K_w|, proving (2).
Only the selected source fibers are used in the lower bound; all other
original fibers are retained in mu and can only improve it.

For a vertex w, a real base functional ell strictly exposes w among P.
For any x in K_w, take an ordinary through-point cap attaining its own
ordinary depth. Adding a sufficiently large finite positive multiple
of ell(p)-ell(w) to its margin excludes every other compact positive
fiber and leaves the own trace unchanged. Thus the original mixed depth
at (w,x) equals its own ordinary depth, pointwise for all x in K_w.
Taking maxima proves the equality branch of (1).

The local mixed maximum used in the notation is attained: cap masses are
upper semicontinuous in the candidate for every fixed closed cap normal
(by the reverse Fatou inequality), so their infimum is upper
semicontinuous on compact K_w. Alternatively, the stronger fixed-fiber
continuity and finite-tilt attainment results in Sections 1 and 6 of
`candidate b989614dc4f86228` apply. This attainment is not
needed for constructing the strictly improved point (5).

## 3. Explicit gain from volume and radius bounds alone

The two inballs in Section 1 can themselves be chosen quantitatively.
Let

    L0=omega R^(d-1),    r0=Gamma_d nu/L0.                   (11)

At the centroid c_B of any selected body B, ordinary Grunbaum gives
at least Gamma_d|B|>=Gamma_d nu to every containing cap. The same lower
bound holds at the ordinary deepest point g of K_w. For every unit u,
write h=h_B(u)-u dot c_B, or h=h_(K_w)(u)-u dot g. The corresponding
cap is contained in a support strip of width h. Its volume is at most
L0 h by the section-area bound. Therefore h>=r0 for every u. Intersecting
all support halfspaces proves

    B_d(c_B,r0) subset B,   B_d(g,r0) subset K_w.             (12)

Take m=sum_i lambda_i c_(K_(p_i)). Minkowski addition of the balls in
(12) gives B_d(m,r0) subset E. Therefore all of (4)--(6) hold with

    r=rho=r0.                                               (13)

These explicit constants depend only on d, k, R, nu. If desired one
may replace k+1 by n+2 in L, weakening the bound uniformly over every
Caratheodory representation. In particular, fixed positive source-volume
and radius bounds give a uniform strict gap, even if base coordinates
are unbounded or the anchored coefficients tend to zero. This is an
absolute-depth statement; dividing the gain by an unbounded original
TOTAL mass does not produce a global OC gap.

Different containing-ball centers in this result are important: no
unauthorized separate translations of the actual fibers are performed.
Their true positions enter (7) through the actual Minkowski body E,
which lies inside K_w. The inequalities are simply invariant under
translating any ball used to estimate a section area.

## 4. A check and a necessary limitation

The exact interval family

    K_-1=K_1=[0,t],  K_0=[0,1],  0<t<=1/3,

is induced by a convex pentagon and has a nonvertex middle base. Its
ordinary middle maximum is 1/2. The exact cap computation in
`candidate a57c113e8e14cc38`, after
scaling by t, gives local mixed maximum (1+t)/2. Thus the improvement is
strict but tends to zero with the source volumes. There is no strictly
positive dimension-only multiple of |K_w| that can be added in (1).

For a rational check of the explicit constants instead use endpoint
intervals [0,1] and middle interval [0,5]. With R=5/2, nu=1, d=1 and
k=2, (11)--(13) give r=rho=1/2, g=5/2, m=1/2,

    delta=1/20, epsilon=1/600, G=1/2400,
    y=749/300.

The exact all-cap formula gives depth 751/300, larger than
A(K_0)+G=5/2+1/2400. The companion Fraction verifier checks these
constants and the old closed-cap formulas at the new point.

The theorem is a strict local source-coupling fact. It neither bounds
the number of positive bases nor proves that some own fiber has the
volume needed to pay the original total-mass OC target.

## 5. Exact equality classification when there are at most 2^n positive bases

Assume now that N=|P|<=2^n, and let M=sum_(p in P)|K_p|. The ordinary
heavy-fiber argument gives the global normalized bound Gamma_d/2^n.
Within this limited-cardinality class its equality cases can be classified
completely:

    max original mixed depth = Gamma_d/2^n

if and only if all four conditions hold:

1. N=2^n;
2. all positive fiber volumes are equal;
3. every p in P is a vertex of conv(P);
4. every K_p is a d-simplex.

For necessity, a largest fiber has volume at least M/N. If N<2^n, or if
N=2^n but the volumes are unequal, its ordinary Grunbaum lower bound is
strictly greater than the target. Thus equality forces conditions 1--2.
By the ordinary theorem proved in
`candidate e2c55c91458e1e8c`, a nonsimplex has
ordinary maximal depth strictly above Gamma_d times its volume, forcing
condition 4. The strict branch of (1) forces condition 3.

Conversely, vertex isolation makes original mixed depth on each fiber
exactly its ordinary depth, pointwise. A simplex has ordinary maximal
depth Gamma_d times its volume. Conditions 1--4 therefore give exactly
Gamma_d/2^n, with no restriction that the simplices have the same shape,
orientation, or centroid.

This includes actual convex families with additional zero-d-volume
fibers in the original body: their integer bases lie outside conv(P),
because an anchored positive-fiber Minkowski combination would force a
positive d-volume fiber at any integer base inside conv(P). Strict base
separation therefore gives zero depth to such additional candidates.

In particular, under conditions 1--4, conv(P) has exactly its vertices
as lattice points. The finite-support equality question about a heavy
base hyperplane is precisely an incidence question for empty lattice
polytopes with 2^n vertices. The statement here gives no reduction of a
general source with more than 2^n positive bases to this class.
